texts.text:
<definition id="fs-id1167132283419">
<term>moment of inertia</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167132283425">rotational mass of rigid bodies that relates to how easy or hard it will be to change the angular velocity of the rotating rigid body</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167132283430">
<term>rotational kinetic energy</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167132205291">kinetic energy due to the rotation of an object; this is part of its total kinetic energy</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167132312261">
<term>lever arm</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167133606817">perpendicular distance from the line that the force vector lies on to a given axis</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167133606821">
<term>torque</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167132306479">cross product of a force and a lever arm to a given axis</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167131118823">
<term>Newton’s second law for rotation</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167131118830">sum of the torques on a rotating system equals its moment of inertia times its angular acceleration</meaning>
</definition>

<note id="fs-id1167134886602">
<title>Newton’s Second Law for Rotation</title>
<para id="fs-id1167134511100">If more than one torque acts on a rigid body about a fixed axis, then the sum of the torques equals the moment of inertia times the angular acceleration:</para>
<equation id="fs-id1167134508536"><m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>τ</m:mi><m:mi>net</m:mi></m:msub><m:mo>=</m:mo><m:mstyle displaystyle="true"><m:munder><m:mo>∑</m:mo><m:mi>i</m:mi></m:munder><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>τ</m:mi><m:mi>i</m:mi></m:msub></m:mrow></m:mstyle><m:mo>=</m:mo><m:mi>I</m:mi><m:mi>α</m:mi><m:mo>.</m:mo></m:mrow></m:math></equation>
</note>

<definition id="fs-id1165037215309"><term>angular momentum</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165037215313">rotational analog of linear momentum, found by taking the product of moment of inertia and angular velocity</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165037004448">
<term>law of conservation of angular momentum</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165037075507">angular momentum is conserved, that is, the initial angular momentum is equal to the final angular momentum when no external torque is applied to the system</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1163713557656">
<term>equilibrium</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1163713525583">body is in equilibrium when its linear and angular accelerations are both zero relative to an inertial frame of reference</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1163713530656">
<term>first equilibrium condition</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1163713428816">expresses translational equilibrium; all external forces acting on the body balance out and their vector sum is zero</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1163709759627">
<term>second equilibrium condition</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1163709750024">expresses rotational equilibrium; all torques due to external forces acting on the body balance out and their vector sum is zero</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1163709774761">
<term>static equilibrium</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1163713276572">body is in static equilibrium when it is at rest in our selected inertial frame of reference</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1168328252700">
<term>universal gravitational constant</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1168328252706">constant representing the strength of the gravitational force, that is believed to be the same throughout the universe</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1168328193986">
<term>Newton’s law of gravitation</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1168327988168">every mass attracts every other mass with a force proportional to the product of their masses, inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them, and with direction along the line connecting the center of mass of each</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1168329517229">
<term>Kepler’s first law</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1168326765861">law stating that every planet moves along an ellipse, with the Sun located at a focus of the ellipse</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1168326790250">
<term>Kepler’s second law</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1168329461373">law stating that a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times, meaning it has a constant areal velocity</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1168329137868">
<term>Kepler’s third law</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1168329188942">law stating that the square of the period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of the orbit</meaning>
</definition>
